readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then std::strcmp with the text 1, in dice_child_context(). The public wrapper is dice_grant_active() (src/system/system.cpp:124).

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 turns grant mode on. Every other text is off. The text is compared, not parsed as a number.
variables.default: Unset: grant mode is off. System options from the command line and from SYSTEM_CONFIG are parsed with no check against a Dice grant.
variables.empty_value: Same as unset: grant mode is off.
variables.invalid_value: Any text other than 1 is off. Examples: 0, true, yes, 01, or 1 with a space. There is no error and no log line.
variables.effect: Tells the C++ startup code that the Dice daemon (the tool that hands out slices of the server to jobs) started this process. In grant mode the code requires DICE_SLOTS, DICE_GRANT_ID and DICE_GRANT_TOKEN to be set and not empty, and it requires a SYSTEM_CONFIG with an --instance that matches the granted slots. It rejects any placement option that asks for resources outside the grant.
variables.interactions: 1. Needs DICE_SLOTS, DICE_GRANT_ID, DICE_GRANT_TOKEN (src/system/system.cpp:128-133). 2. pos_startup_host parses SYSTEM_CONFIG even when it is unset, and fails without --instance (src/pos/driver.cpp:208-224, src/pos/fake.cpp:99-115). 3. --instance, --resource-map, --devices, --app-cores, --dev-cores, --helper-cores, --numa, --tracer-core and --hugepage_file are checked against the grant, from the command line and from SYSTEM_CONFIG (src/system/system.cpp:1785-1865). 4. POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH and --hugepage_file must resolve to /dev/hugepages/libpos (src/system/system.cpp:1649-1661). 5. The trusted resource map is read only from /opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml (src/system/system.cpp:1681-1682). 6. system_optimize only pins the application threads. --no-opt does not stop that (src/system/system.cpp:1339-1345). 7. Peer CPU choice and NUMA memory policy follow the real sibling CPUs and NUMA node numbers (src/system/system.cpp:416-438, 450-459, 763-776). The value is read again at each call. It is not cached. The Python launchers test the same name with the same rule: bin/rinzler:475, bin/runtron:494, bin/slice:5097. The Dice daemon sets it to 1 for every child (bin/dice:3657).
variables.how_to_check: No log line says that grant mode is on. Signs of grant mode: startup logs 'INIT: environment system config: <text>' even when SYSTEM_CONFIG is unset (src/pos/driver.cpp:210). Failures log 'Dice grant <id>: <option> requested '<value>'; permitted <...>. Remove this override or request an instance with compatible resources.' (src/system/system.cpp:1641-1643), or 'Incomplete Dice grant environment; launch through Dice again' (src/system/system.cpp:1667), or 'INIT: Dice grant requires SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance' (src/pos/driver.cpp:221).
variables.audience_reason: It changes how deployed rinzler and runtron accept placement options. The Dice daemon sets it. A person should check it, not set it by hand.

readers.program: libsystem (static library 'system', src/system/CMakeLists.txt:19-34; linked into rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host and the tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in dice_grant_env_complete(). Tests that the value is set and not empty.

variables.values: Comma-separated list of slot numbers. Each item is a decimal integer of 0 or more. Not accepted by the C++ parser: spaces, a plus sign, a range such as 0-3, an empty item, a comma at the end. The order is free: the code sorts the list (src/system/system.cpp:1509, 1673). The sorted slots must be one unbroken run. The run length must divide the total slot count. The first slot must be a multiple of the run length. The last slot must be below the total (src/system/system.cpp:1689-1696).
variables.default: Not read unless DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is exactly 1. The two C++ functions that read it (dice_grant_env_complete and the functions below) are reached only in grant mode. In grant mode an unset value fails startup with 'Incomplete Dice grant environment; launch through Dice again' (src/system/system.cpp:1667).
variables.empty_value: Same as unset. In grant mode startup fails with the 'Incomplete Dice grant environment' message.
variables.invalid_value: Text that does not parse: 'Dice grant <id>: DICE_SLOTS requested 'invalid'; permitted slot IDs. ...' (src/system/system.cpp:1672) or 'Invalid DICE_SLOTS for Dice grant' (src/system/system.cpp:1504). Slots that do not form one supported instance: 'DICE_SLOTS requested '[...]'; permitted one supported contiguous instance within 0-<last slot>' (src/system/system.cpp:1695-1696), or 'permitted trusted map shapes' (src/system/system.cpp:1703-1704), or 'permitted supported fallback shapes' (src/system/system.cpp:1706-1707). Startup fails in each case.
variables.effect: Names the slots that the Dice daemon granted to this process. A slot is one equal share of the server (FPGA cards, CPU cores, memory). The C++ code works out the one --instance that the slots form: instance id = first slot / run length, instance count = total slots / run length (src/system/system.cpp:1697-1698). It takes the permitted cards, CPU cores and NUMA nodes for these slots from the trusted resource map, or from the built-in table when no map matches (src/system/system.cpp:1699-1708).
variables.interactions: Read only in grant mode (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1). The --instance in SYSTEM_CONFIG must describe the same slots. If not, startup fails with 'Dice grant <id>: --instance requested '<x,y>'; permitted --instance <a>,<b> (slots [...])' (src/system/system.cpp:1789-1795) or 'SYSTEM_CONFIG --instance does not match DICE_SLOTS' (src/system/system.cpp:1512). The Python tools parse the same variable with looser rules. bin/slice accepts ranges such as 0-7 and spaces (parse_slot_mask, bin/slice:1115-1138). bin/rinzler accepts spaces and empty items (bin/rinzler:507-516). The C++ parser rejects those forms. The Dice daemon writes the canonical form: slot numbers joined with commas (bin/dice:3656).
variables.how_to_check: On success the instance worked out from the slots shows in 'Configured instance <id>,<count> using resource map (<path>).' (src/system/system.cpp:1986) or 'Configured instance <id>,<count> using hardcoded settings.' (src/system/system.cpp:1989). These lines also appear without Dice. The slot list itself is printed only in the error lines listed under invalid_value.
variables.audience_reason: Read by deployed rinzler and runtron in grant mode. It decides which cards, cores and memory nodes the process may use. The Dice daemon sets it.

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (src/pos/CMakeLists.txt:4-22; linked into rinzler and runtron through full_scheduler_static, and into hardware tests). Not in pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host)

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi. Only a value above 0 is used. The unit is queries in one hardware attention pass.
variables.default: Unset: the cap is the value computed for the card: min(metadata limit, maximum_batch_size). The metadata limit is 256 entries / 4 subpasses = 64 queries (h/pos/config.hpp:43, h/libpos.hpp:38). maximum_batch_size is at most MAX_B = 32 queries (h/libpos.hpp:33, src/pos/driver.cpp:1581-1588).
variables.empty_value: Same as unset. atoi gives 0, and 0 is not used.
variables.invalid_value: 0, a negative number or non-numeric text is the same as unset. There is no error and no log line. A value above the computed cap has no effect.
variables.effect: Lowers the largest number of queries that one hardware attention pass carries on a card. The result is min(value, computed cap) (src/pos/driver.cpp:1617). The variable cannot raise the cap.
variables.interactions: The model code uses the result to split queries into passes (h/tron/models/model.hpp:3046-3050). The worker asserts that each request stays within it (src/pos/worker.cpp:822-827). It matters only when hardware attention is in use. The value is read once per process: a change needs a restart. The pos_fake version of the function does not read the variable (src/pos/fake.cpp:415-418). No setter and no document names it in the checkout.
variables.how_to_check: none found. The cap is printed only when the worker assertion fails: '... HW attention batch size <B> exceeds cap <cap> ...' (src/pos/worker.cpp:823-827).
variables.audience_reason: No document and no setter in the checkout. It can only lower a batch cap. It reads as an experiment setting, not as a supported tuning setting.

variables.name: HWATTN_WLR

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (src/pos/CMakeLists.txt:4-22; linked into rinzler and runtron through full_scheduler_static, and into hardware tests). Not in pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host)
readers.mechanism: hwattn_env_override("HWATTN_WLR") in PosDevice::init. The helper calls std::getenv(env_name) at src/pos/device.cpp:103, then std::atoi at line 105. The result is kept in a function-local static.

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi. A value above 0 forces the feature on. Every other set value forces it off.
variables.default: Unset: each card decides from its bitfile (the FPGA image) with hwattn_wlr_bitfile_ok (h/pos/device.hpp:780-795). Project 01 needs version 05.08 or later. Project 03 needs version 05.08 or later and a release date of 2026-05-18 or later. Other projects: off.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. An empty value forces the feature OFF, because atoi gives 0.
variables.invalid_value: 0, a negative number or non-numeric text forces the feature off. There is no error. The log line below reports the forced state.
variables.effect: Forces hardware attention weight-load reuse (WLR) on or off for every card, in place of the bitfile check. With WLR on, when an attention command repeats the weight commands of the previous attention command, the worker sends one K and V command pair that tells the FPGA to reuse the weights it already loaded (src/pos/worker.cpp:1380-1403).
variables.interactions: The value is read at the first PosDevice::init and kept for the life of the process. Forcing it on for a bitfile that lacks WLR is not guarded by the code. The model code still logs 'Dev <addr>: bitfile does not support HW attention WLR; update to ...' from the bitfile check alone (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1869-1875). That line ignores the override, so it can appear while WLR is forced on. TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING uses the same helper and the same rules (src/pos/device.cpp:216-217). Not read by pos_fake programs.
variables.how_to_check: When the variable is set, the driver logs once per process at info level: 'HW attention: HWATTN_WLR=<value> forces the feature ON by env flag; the bitfile capability check is bypassed' (or OFF) (src/pos/device.cpp:106-108). The FUSE stats counter /rinzler/stats/devices/<index>/wcmd_reuse/attn counts the reuse commands that a card sent (src/pos/device.cpp:693-694, src/pos/worker.cpp:1403). It stays at 0 while WLR is off.
variables.audience_reason: It bypasses a hardware capability check and no document names it. The code comment calls it a feature switch (h/pos/device.hpp:433-436), so the value 0 could serve an operator as an off switch. That use is a judgement.

variables.name: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (src/pos/CMakeLists.txt:4-22; linked into rinzler and runtron through full_scheduler_static, and into hardware tests). Not in pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host)
readers.mechanism: getenv in pos_startup_host(), then atoi at lines 260 and 262, or at line 267

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi: the number of 1 GiB hugepages for each NUMA node of the server. The code counts one NUMA node per CPU package (socket) (get_num_numa_nodes, src/system/system.cpp:300-307). There is no range check.
variables.default: Unset: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is used when it is set. Otherwise the count is the --nr_hugepages value from SYSTEM_CONFIG or the command line, or 16 hugepages (default_n_hugepages, h/system/config.hpp:12).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. An empty value counts as set: atoi gives 0, the page count becomes 0, and POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is not read. A count of 0: by reading the code, the hugepage file is mapped with length 0, the mapping fails, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:602-605). This was derived by reading. It was not run.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text is read as 0. A count of 0: by reading the code, the hugepage file is mapped with length 0, the mapping fails, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:602-605). This was derived by reading. It was not run. A negative value becomes a very large unsigned count. The memlock cap then lowers it to the limit. There is no error message for a bad value.
variables.effect: Sets how many 1 GiB hugepages the process maps for its DMA heap (the memory that the FPGA cards read and write). With --instance: pages = value x NUMA node count / 8 x slices owned by this instance, in integer arithmetic from left to right (src/pos/driver.cpp:260). Example: value 48, 2 NUMA nodes, an instance with 4 slices: 48 x 2 / 8 x 4 = 48 pages. Without --instance: pages = value (src/pos/driver.cpp:267).
variables.interactions: Wins over POS_NR_HUGEPAGES (else-if at src/pos/driver.cpp:272). Wins over --nr_hugepages from SYSTEM_CONFIG and from the command line, because it is assigned later (order listed at src/system/huge.cpp:61-68). The divisor 8 is the constant n_slices (h/system/system.hpp:212). It is not the slot count of the server. The result is capped by the locked-memory limit of the process (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in GiB, src/pos/driver.cpp:277-281). With --instance that limit is first rounded down to a multiple of the slices owned (src/pos/driver.cpp:264). The packaged rinzler unit sets LimitMEMLOCK=infinity (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:60). The hugepage count also sets a KV cache default. Legacy allocator mode: with no KV cache size given, the KV cache target is half of the count, in GiB (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455-458). The comment at h/system/memory.hpp:69-73 says this can be the count before the cap. Arena allocator mode: that target is made inert (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-70), and the host eviction target defaults to about 95% of the final pool (src/system/memory.cpp:195-205). The comment at src/system/huge.cpp:70 names this variable as the one to use in production. Not read by pos_fake programs.
variables.how_to_check: With --instance, info line 'INIT: hugepages <count> (per numa <value>, per slice <n>)' (src/pos/driver.cpp:261-262). The last number is the number of slices that the instance owns, not pages per slice. Without --instance, debug line 'INIT: using POS_1GB_PER_NUMA without instances configured. hugepages <count>' (src/pos/driver.cpp:268-270). When the cap applies, warning 'INIT: hugepages capped by ulimit constraints to <limit> of <count> available.' (src/pos/driver.cpp:278-279). Debug line 'INIT: Allocating <count> hugepages from <path>* on numa <node>' (src/system/memory.cpp:158-159). With the arena allocator, the FUSE stats file /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/hugepages shows the final budget after the cap (src/system/memory.cpp:634-639). In the legacy allocator mode, with no KV cache size given, 'Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache (covering all models)' prints half of the count (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455-457). The log level is debug when TRON_LOG_LEVEL is unset (src/system/spdlog.cpp:39-42).
variables.audience_reason: It sizes the heap memory of deployed rinzler and runtron. The code comment recommends it for production.
variables.disagreement: Not wrong, but vague in two places. 1. The inventory says non-numeric text is read as 0. It does not say that an EMPTY value counts as set: the count becomes 0 and POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is ignored (src/pos/driver.cpp:249, 272). It also does not say what a count of 0 does. 2. cpp-pos-system.json says the default KV cache size is half of the hugepage count. That holds only in the legacy allocator mode. In arena allocator mode the target is inert (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-70). cpp-rinzler-runtron.json has the qualifier.

variables.values: Path of a file on a hugetlbfs mount (a file system that hands out hugepages). The text is used as given. The path needs a directory part.
variables.default: Unset: the path from --hugepage_file (SYSTEM_CONFIG or command line), or /dev/hugepages/libpos (default_hugepage_file, h/system/config.hpp:6).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset: the path becomes empty. Outside grant mode, by reading the code, startup then fails in pos_heap_setup: the cleanup step cannot read the empty directory name, logs 'Hugepage cleanup cannot read : ...' (src/system/huge.cpp:258-266), and pos_heap_setup returns -1 with 'Hugepage slices for this configuration are still owned by another process; ...' (src/system/memory.cpp:149-155). This was derived by reading. It was not run. In grant mode an empty value fails with the 'Dice grant <id>: POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH requested ...' error (src/system/system.cpp:1655-1660).
variables.invalid_value: A path whose directory cannot be read fails startup with the two messages listed under empty_value. A bare file name with no directory part has an empty directory name and fails the same way (path.parent_path(), src/system/huge.cpp:260). not determined: the result of a path that is not on hugetlbfs (looked at src/system/huge.cpp:521-541).
variables.effect: Sets the base path of the hugepage file that backs the DMA heap. Without --instance the process maps this one file. With --instance only the directory of the path is used: the files are <directory>/slice-<k>-of-8, one for each slice that the instance owns (src/system/huge.cpp:639-643, 670-672). Startup cleanup removes unused hugepage files that match this path or sit in its directory (src/system/huge.cpp:97-107, 691-718).
variables.interactions: Wins over --hugepage_file from SYSTEM_CONFIG and from the command line, because it is assigned later (src/pos/driver.cpp:283-288, order listed at src/system/huge.cpp:74-78). In grant mode (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the path must resolve to the same file as /dev/hugepages/libpos (std::filesystem::weakly_canonical, src/system/system.cpp:1649-1661). The default path is then the one used (src/pos/driver.cpp:286-287). The apply step at src/pos/driver.cpp:283 runs only in the real driver. pos_fake programs reach only the grant check at src/system/system.cpp:2089.
variables.how_to_check: Debug line 'INIT: Allocating <count> hugepages from <path>* on numa <node>' (src/system/memory.cpp:158-159). In grant mode a rejected path logs 'Dice grant <id>: POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH requested '<path>'; permitted cleanup base '/dev/hugepages/libpos' (equivalent canonical paths are supported). ...' (src/system/system.cpp:1641-1643, 1657-1660).
variables.audience_reason: It selects where deployed rinzler and runtron keep their hugepage files. A wrong value stops startup.
variables.disagreement: Not wrong, but one gap. cpp-pos-system.json says 'not determined: the result of an empty path outside a Dice grant'. The code answers it: both cleanup functions scan path.parent_path() (src/system/huge.cpp:260, 453, 711). For an empty path, and for a bare file name, that directory name is empty, the scan fails, and pos_heap_setup returns -1 (src/system/memory.cpp:149-155). Derived by reading, not run.

variables.name: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (src/pos/CMakeLists.txt:4-22; linked into rinzler and runtron through full_scheduler_static, and into hardware tests). Not in pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host)
readers.mechanism: getenv in pos_startup_host(), then atoi at line 273

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi: the total number of 1 GiB hugepages for this process. There is no range check.
variables.default: Unset: the count is the --nr_hugepages value from SYSTEM_CONFIG or the command line, or 16 hugepages (default_n_hugepages, h/system/config.hpp:12).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. An empty value counts as set: atoi gives 0 and the page count becomes 0. A count of 0: by reading the code, the hugepage file is mapped with length 0, the mapping fails, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:602-605). This was derived by reading. It was not run.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text is read as 0. A count of 0: by reading the code, the hugepage file is mapped with length 0, the mapping fails, and TRON_ASSERT(store != MAP_FAILED) stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:602-605). This was derived by reading. It was not run. A negative value becomes a very large unsigned count. The memlock cap then lowers it to the limit. There is no error message for a bad value.
variables.effect: Sets how many 1 GiB hugepages the process maps for its DMA heap (the memory that the FPGA cards read and write). The value is the count for the whole process. It is not divided by slices or NUMA nodes.
variables.interactions: Ignored when POS_1GB_PER_NUMA is set, even to an empty value (else-if at src/pos/driver.cpp:272). Wins over --nr_hugepages from SYSTEM_CONFIG and from the command line, because it is assigned later (order listed at src/system/huge.cpp:61-68). The result is capped by the locked-memory limit of the process (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in GiB, src/pos/driver.cpp:277-281). With --instance the final count must divide evenly by the number of slices owned, or TRON_ASSERT_EQ stops the process (src/system/huge.cpp:665-666). In this branch the cap is not rounded to the slice count. The hugepage count also sets a KV cache default. Legacy allocator mode: with no KV cache size given, the KV cache target is half of the count, in GiB (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455-458). The comment at h/system/memory.hpp:69-73 says this can be the count before the cap. Arena allocator mode: that target is made inert (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-70), and the host eviction target defaults to about 95% of the final pool (src/system/memory.cpp:195-205). The comment at src/system/huge.cpp:65 and 71 calls this variable deprecated and spells it POS_NR_HUGEPAGE. The code reads POS_NR_HUGEPAGES. Not read by pos_fake programs. bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py:216 sets it for a child process.
variables.how_to_check: Debug line 'INIT: using POS_NR_HUGEPAGES. hugepages <count>' (src/pos/driver.cpp:274). When the cap applies, warning 'INIT: hugepages capped by ulimit constraints to <limit> of <count> available.' (src/pos/driver.cpp:278-279). Debug line 'INIT: Allocating <count> hugepages from <path>* on numa <node>' (src/system/memory.cpp:158-159). With the arena allocator, the FUSE stats file /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/hugepages shows the final budget after the cap (src/system/memory.cpp:634-639). In the legacy allocator mode, with no KV cache size given, 'Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache (covering all models)' prints half of the count (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455-457). The log level is debug when TRON_LOG_LEVEL is unset (src/system/spdlog.cpp:39-42).
variables.audience_reason: It sizes the heap memory of deployed rinzler and runtron.
variables.disagreement: Not wrong, but vague. The inventory says non-numeric text is read as 0. It does not say that an EMPTY value counts as set and gives a count of 0, and it does not say what a count of 0 does. It also does not say that an empty POS_1GB_PER_NUMA hides this variable. cpp-rinzler-runtron.json lists call sites that do not read the name as readers (src/rinzler.cpp:4054, h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1488).

readers.program: libtron (static library tron, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:193; linked into rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host and tests): tron::resolve_weights()
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. This is the only site that names the variable in src/, h/ and rust/. Callers reach it through default_model_weights (h/tron/models/registry.hpp:94) and default_model_path (h/tron/models/registry.hpp:101-102).

variables.values: Path to a directory: the root of the model weights tree. The text is used as given.
variables.empty_value: Same as unset (test env[0] != 0 at src/tron/models/load.cpp:45).
variables.invalid_value: When <value>/<model name> does not exist, resolve_weights logs 'Weights not found at the source path: <path>' (src/tron/models/load.cpp:27, 47) and returns an empty path. default_model_weights then stops the process with 'Couldn't find weights directory <name> for model <id>' (h/tron/models/registry.hpp:95-96). Other errors log 'Failed to inspect weights path ...' (src/tron/models/load.cpp:24) or 'Failed to resolve weights path ...' (src/tron/models/load.cpp:53).
variables.effect: Sets the root directory under which a relative model weights name, such as <org>/<model>, is looked up. The found path is made canonical once per call. rinzler and runtron read the weights, config.json, the tokenizer files and the chat template from the resolved directory.
variables.interactions: An absolute weights path does not use the variable (src/tron/models/load.cpp:37-40). rinzler --model-path does not use it: the directory is the fixed text /opt/positron/weights/huggingface/ plus the given subpath (src/rinzler.cpp:1706-1708). runtron --model-path with a relative path uses the same fixed prefix (src/runtron.cpp:665-670). The variable is read on each call, so a change during the run affects later lookups. rinzler resolves the path once at model load and stores it (src/rinzler.cpp:2064-2071). POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE plays no part. Call sites that reach the read: src/rinzler.cpp:1714, 1818, 2071, src/rinzler/model-metadata.cpp:163, src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:2218, h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1471, h/tron/models/cache.hpp:64.
variables.how_to_check: Info line 'Model <id> at <resolved directory> not in cache <pointer>, loading' (h/tron/models/cache.hpp:112-113). In rinzler, GET /v1/info returns a models object that maps each model name to the canonical weights path in use (src/rinzler.cpp:3850-3869).
variables.audience_reason: It selects where deployed rinzler and runtron find model weights. A wrong value stops model loading.

notes: Scope: read-only work on the snapshot at commit 7eddde7895. Nothing was built or run. Step 1 was done before the inventory files were opened. Result: for 11 of the 14 variables the inventory agrees with the code. For 3 (POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH) the inventory is not wrong but vague or has a gap; see the disagreement fields. The task text calls all 14 names variables that product code reads. The code says otherwise for 4 of them, and the inventory already says the same. MIXTRAL_PATH: read only in test code (Rust #[cfg(test)] module and 3 C++ test files). POS_PREQUANT_CACHE and POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE: read by an inline function in a product header, but only t/t_prequant_cache.cpp includes that header at this commit, so no deployed program reads them. PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME: no TRON C, C++ or Rust code names it. The Perfetto SDK is expected to read it, but the SDK source is not in the checkout. Facts that the inventory does not have and that help a support engineer. 1. An empty HWATTN_WLR forces the feature off (the inventory has this). The model code still logs 'bitfile does not support HW attention WLR' from the bitfile check alone (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1869-1875), so that line can appear while WLR is forced on. 2. DICE_SLOTS: the C++ parser is stricter than the Python parsers. bin/slice accepts ranges such as 0-7 (bin/slice:1115-1138). The C++ code rejects them (src/system/system.cpp:1470-1491). 3. The info line at src/pos/driver.cpp:261-262 labels its last number 'per slice', but the number is the count of slices that the instance owns. 4. POS_WEIGHTS_DIR can be checked on a running rinzler with GET /v1/info (src/rinzler.cpp:3850-3869). One more call chain reaches the read: h/tron/models/cache.hpp:64. 5. The log level is debug when TRON_LOG_LEVEL is unset (src/system/spdlog.cpp:39-42), so the debug lines named in how_to_check appear by default. Statements marked 'derived by reading' (a hugepage count of 0, an empty POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH) follow from the code, plus the Linux rule that a mapping of length 0 fails. They were not run. A start of runtron with the value on a test host would confirm them. cpp-rinzler-runtron.json lists call sites as readers in its cross-area entries (for example src/rinzler.cpp:4054, src/rinzler.cpp:4046, src/runtron.cpp:248, h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1488). Those lines do not read the names. A merge should take the reader sites of the owning area. Other variables met in this code are all in the verified inventory: SYSTEM_CONFIG, TRACE_FILE, TRON_HEAP_SHADOW, SUDO_USER, TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR, TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING, USE_HW_ATTN, TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE, RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH, TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES, TRON_LOG_LEVEL, TRON_LOG_DIR, SPDLOG_LEVEL, RZ_KV_CACHE_GB in the three C++ files; PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME, CPUAFFINITY, RZ_CLI_ARGS, DICE_DISABLE, GEMMA4_PATH in other verified files. Stale or misleading text in the repository: src/system/huge.cpp:65-71 spells the name POS_NR_HUGEPAGE; the stat description at src/system/memory.cpp:556-559 says the budget comes from POS_NR_HUGEPAGES only; doc/pos_heap_v2.md:763-767 cites line numbers that no longer match (h/system/config.hpp:10, src/pos/driver.cpp:170-205, src/system/system.cpp:39); README.md:64-66 describes POS_NR_HUGEPAGES as hugepages per NUMA node in /etc/default/positron for a 'positron' service, while the TRON code uses the value as the page count of one process and no file in the checkout reads /etc/default/positron.
